reporting-org.narrative: Obodo Centre for Advocacy and Equal Rights

description.narrative:
The Human Rights Centre, located at No. 22 Ogbunike Street, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos, was officially launched on June 28, 2024, marking a significant milestone in our commitment to providing a safe and inclusive space for marginalized communities in Nigeria. This initiative has been met with overwhelming support and engagement, serving as both a sanctuary and a hub for advocacy, education, and community building.
The lease agreement signed on May 1, 2024, covers a period of three years, with an option to extend for an additional two years, ensuring the long-term availability of this crucial resource. Since its opening, the Human Rights Centre has hosted 10 in-person community events, each of which has contributed significantly to the Centre's mission. These events have covered a range of topics, including legal and human rights, mental health, community building, and cultural expression. Feedback from attendees has been decidedly positive, with many expressing a sense of safety and connection as a result of participating in these events.
To date, a total of 629 individuals have utilized the Centre, availing themselves of the safe space it provides. The Centre's capacity to accommodate up to 150 persons at any given time has allowed it to serve as a hub for community activities, offering a refuge where individuals can engage in meaningful discourse, access resources, and find support. True to its primary intent, the Centre has swiftly become a cornerstone of the community, reinforcing the importance of safe, dedicated spaces in the fight for human rights and equality.
